    A GAME OF GOOD ANGLES
    A QUICK FIELD GUIDE

    A different kind
    of building block.

    Place triangles on a classic 10 × 20 grid. Every triangle uses three boundary points of a 2 × 2 grid, with only horizontal, vertical, or 45° diagonal edges. Grouping rotated copies leaves three distinct families, each with its own color.

    1. You move. The pieces don’t fall.New pieces appear one grid row above the tallest part of the stack. Left, right, and down move one grid unit. Hold a movement key or on-screen arrow for steady movement. Up rotates counterclockwise; W rotates clockwise. A translucent triangle is your current piece.
    2. Make a connection.Touch the floor or any placed piece, even at a single point. Overlap is never allowed. Space places a legal piece where it is; otherwise it moves to the highest legal position supported from below by the floor or another piece, without changing columns. Sideways contact alone won’t stop it.
    3. Keep an eye on the clock.You begin with 10 seconds per piece. Each placement makes the next timer 0.5% shorter, down to 1 second. Time running out uses exactly the same placement rule as Space. Pieces and movement stay on whole grid points.
    4. Leave room to grow.Fill an entire horizontal row to clear it. Touching the top ends the game. If no supported legal position exists in the current column when an illegal piece is placed, the game also ends.

    C holds a piece once per turn, without resetting the clock. P pauses. F toggles fullscreen.
